root_cause.text: The validation check used `>` instead of `>=` when comparing `wire_order[i]` against `ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)`, allowing the value to equal the array size and subsequently be used as an out-of-bounds array index in `config_pins[wire_order[i]]`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes line 88 from `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))` to `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] >= ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))`. Since `config_pins` has 4 elements with valid indices 0-3, `ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)` equals 4. The original check only rejected values greater than 4 (i.e., 5+), but allowed the value 4 to pass validation, which is then used as an array index causing out-of-bounds access. The fix correctly rejects any value >= 4, ensuring only valid indices 0-3 are permitted.
